Florida has reported nearly 500 dengue cases this year, including more than 250 infections acquired within the state, as new University of Florida research points to residential yards in Indian River County as a key place to understand mosquito-bite exposure. The Florida Department of Health’s latest weekly surveillance report , covering Sept. 20-26, lists 252 locally acquired dengue cases and 245 travel-associated cases statewide 497 total. The locally acquired cases were reported in Hillsborough, Miami-Dade, Orange, Palm Beach, Pasco, Pinellas and Polk counties. Palm Beach County had one locally acquired case and 12 travel-associated cases; St. Lucie County had six travel-associated cases. No locally acquired dengue cases were listed for Indian River County in the report. The state’s locally acquired total includes 223 cases in Hillsborough County, the center of Florida’s outbreak. Health officials also reported 20 mosquito pools testing positive for dengue statewide. Nationally, the CDC’s most recent weekly provisional report counted 690 dengue cases among U.S. Florida accounted for 403 of those cases in the CDC reporting system, though the state’s more current surveillance report lists a higher total because reporting systems update on different schedules. Against that backdrop, researchers at UF/IFAS’ Florida Medical Entomology Laboratory in Vero Beach found a surprising mosquito pattern in suburban Indian River County. The team expected residential yards to be dominated by Aedes albopictus , also known as the Asian tiger mosquito. Instead, researchers found relatively high numbers of Aedes aegypti the yellow fever mosquito and one of the two species most closely associated with dengue transmission worldwide. The finding does not mean dengue is circulating in Indian River County . But it underscores why backyard mosquito control and personal bite prevention matter, researchers said. See also: Florida stages emergency supplies as Tropical Storm Isaias strengthens in Gulf The first-of-its-kind study paired mosquito trapping at homes with a smartphone-based Bite Diary that let residents document when and where they were bitten. Researchers collected 3,788 female mosquitoes from 78 yards. Of 70 reported bites, nearly 93% happened outdoors and nearly 74% happened at home, according to the peer-reviewed study . The number of mosquitoes trapped in a yard was not associated with the number of bites residents reported. Instead, people who spent more time outside during the evening, from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m., reported more bites. Gardening and walking dogs were among activities commonly reported when bites occurred. Dengue is spread when an infected mosquito bites a person; it does not spread directly from person to person. Symptoms can include fever, severe muscle and joint pain, rash, nausea and pain behind the eyes. People with symptoms should contact a health care provider, especially after travel to an area where dengue is common. Health officials urge residents to use EPA-registered insect repellent, wear long sleeves and pants when practical, repair window and door screens, and dump standing water from containers such as buckets, flowerpots, toys, tires and pool covers.

As Florida voters prepare to decide Amendment 3 on Nov. 3, residents, elected officials and policy experts gathered in Palm Beach County to discuss how the proposed constitutional amendment could affect homeowners, local governments and public services.WATCH: WPTV Let's Hear It: Property Tax Town Hall on Amendment 3 (Part 1)The discussion took place during WPTV's "Let's Hear It" community event and town hall at Palm Beach State College's Lake Worth Beach campus, where attendees asked questions and heard arguments from both supporters and opponents of the referendum.For many voters, the amendment could have significant financial implications. Supporters argue it would provide property tax relief for homeowners, while critics warn it could reduce funding for local services and shift key decisions to future lawmakers.WATCH: WPTV Let's Hear It: Property Tax Town Hall on Amendment 3 (Part 2)The evening began with WPTV's "Let's Hear It" event, giving residents an opportunity to learn more about the amendment before voting.Rich Bartholomew, advocacy chair for the League of Women Voters, said he appreciated the effort to help residents better understand the proposal."I have been watching everything that WPTV has been doing on this," Bartholomew said. "I think this is a very important event."Bartholomew also expressed concern that voters may not fully understand the long-term consequences of the amendment based solely on what appears on the ballot."There's nothing showing you on your ballot how all these things, these dominoes would fall," he said.Some residents in attendance said they support Amendment 3 because of rising property tax costs.John, a Palm Beach County resident, argued that continued increases in residential tax bills are becoming increasingly difficult for homeowners to manage."If you think about the tax we're paying now, where's it going to be in five years or 10 years at the rate we keep growing the tax on residences?" he said. "It's unsustainable."Rosey Gekas, another supporter of the amendment, said local governments should focus on budgeting and spending accountability."The scare tactics that I'm continuously hearing is just beyond," Gekas said. "The last five years, the amount of money that has come in from property taxes is skyrocketing. Where is all that money going? We just need to budget."WATCH: Residents, elected officials and policy experts talk Amendment 3 at WPTV Let's Hear It eventSeveral elected officials speaking during the town hall urged voters to consider how reduced tax revenues could affect essential government functions.West Palm Beach Mayor Keith James said the amendment could result in significant financial losses for municipalities."You have to factor in the impact on services," James said.According to James, the City of West Palm Beach could lose $21.7 million in the first year and more than $31 million during the first two years if the measure passes.State Sen. Tina Polsky also raised concerns about potential long-term consequences."This is unchangeable," Polsky said. "If we make this huge mistake on Nov. 3, we are stuck with it forever."Polsky argued that future legislative decisions tied to the amendment could expand its effects beyond what voters initially expect.Supporters of the amendment included state lawmakers who said homeowners deserve relief from rising costs.Florida Rep. Toby Overdorf said homeowners could see significant savings if the amendment is approved."They deserve money back in their pockets," Overdorf said. "Anywhere from $1,700 to as much as $4,000. That's what we're looking at."Amendment 3 will appear on Florida's Nov. Like all proposed constitutional amendments in Florida, it must receive at least 60% voter approval to be adopted into the state constitution.WPTV will continue covering the amendment and providing resources for voters seeking information ahead of Election Day.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

No arrests have been made in the shooting death of a 17-year-old at a teen meetup near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County, with a self-defense claim expected in the case, Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced Monday.WATCH BELOW: Sheriff Eric Flowers give update on shooting death of teen"We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," Flowers said.The shooting occurred late Friday night when approximately 100 teens, ranging in age from 14 to 19, gathered at Garcia's Boat Ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512, the sheriff said. Deputies had broken up a similar group earlier that evening before the crowd moved to the boat ramp."The 17-year-old, and a group of his friends, are approaching a truck, and there are two people, both 18 years old, inside of that truck. The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch," Flowers said. "He's going to punch on the people that are inside of that truck. That shot is the shot that ultimately killed 17-year-old in this case."The teen's friends drove him away from the scene, east on County Road 512, while calling 911 and a dispatcher told them to stop at Fellsmere City Hall, where emergency crews performed CPR, the sheriff said. He was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries.The two individuals in the truck were identified using the sheriff's office's Flock technology, the sheriff said. Flowers said both have been cooperative with investigators, surrendering the weapon used in the shooting and the truck. Additional individuals involved in the incident have also been identified through Flock, though some remain unidentified. Investigators also recovered other weapons from the vehicle in which the 17-year-old was transported from the scene.WATCH: 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat RampFlowers said a warrant will be submitted in the case, but it will be up to the state to determine whether charges are filed."There have been no arrests on this case at this time, because the preliminary investigation shows that the 17-year-old was opening the door to attempt to fight with the two that were inside of the vehicle. They had a history of fighting," Flowers said. "Self defense plays a part in these, and when these kids go out and videotape these fights, and now guns are involved, there's going to be more of this." Names of those involved are not being released as the investigation continues, the sheriff said.Investigators believe at least four fights occurred at the boat ramp on the night of the shooting. Multiple shell casings and rounds were recovered from the scene.During Monday's news conference, Flowers released video of the shooting, noting the footage had already circulated widely on social media and that the victim's mother had seen it. One of the 18-year-olds involved in the shooting attends Vero Beach High School.The sheriff said teen meetups like the one at Garcia's Boat Ramp are coordinated through Snapchat, making them difficult for law enforcement to track in advance."When it's Snapchat, it's basically a private conversation," Flowers said. "But it quickly can escalate to over 100, 150, 200 people there."Flowers said the meetups, which have included alcohol, fighting, and firearms, have been taking place for years across Indian River County, Okeechobee, and surrounding areas, but that social media has intensified the danger."Now we're adding guns and alcohol into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix, and so what we're seeing is an escalation of each one of these," Flowers said. There's guns, and those two just don't mix. And now add in the fuel of the fire of social media, and now we have a 17-year-old dead."The sheriff said teens at these gatherings are motivated in part by a desire for online attention."The kids like to fight, and they like to videotape it, and they like to get their likes and shares because of that," Flowers said. Parents, you see these videos. You do not want your teens out at these meetups."With Vero Beach High School's homecoming game scheduled for Friday and the dance on Saturday, Flowers said additional deputies will be on duty. Meanwhile, the sheriff urged parents to monitor their children's whereabouts and report any information about planned meetups to the sheriff's office."Parents, if your kids are telling you that they're headed out to one of these meetups, ask them where they're going. Ask, find out the details. Share that with us," Flowers said.He recommended parents use location-sharing apps such as Life360 to track their children and said a child appearing to be in a remote or unusual location can be an indicator that a meetup is taking place.The investigation remains active. Flowers said anyone who witnessed any of the events that night, including the shooting itself, and has not yet spoken to investigators is urged to come forward."I can tell you, our investigation is not even remotely over, and if we are able to identify people that were involved in this, from underage drinking to fighting, hurting other people," Flowers said. " If they did something wrong, they're going to have to be accountable for that."Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Man Arrested in August Shooting Death of Ex-Girlfriend
hero.body:
A 33-year-old Vero Beach man has been arrested on a first-degree murder charge in the August shooting death of his former girlfriend, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Matthew Allen Waggle was taken into custody Oct. 5 on an active warrant and is being held without bond in connection with the killing of Dawn Marie Kriskewic.

Deputies responded to the 500 block of 1st Street in Vero Beach after 911 callers reported a woman lying in the roadway. They found Kriskewic with injuries consistent with gunshot wounds and began CPR before she was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.

Investigators identified Waggle as Kriskewic's former boyfriend. A coworker told detectives that Kriskewic had expressed concerns about Waggle before her death and that he had previously threatened consequences if she called police when he came to retrieve his belongings. Surveillance footage reviewed by detectives showed a person identified as Waggle near the area around the time of the shooting, and additional footage showed him walking through the area before and after it. Investigators said footage also showed him discarding a shirt, which they later recovered.

Investigators recovered a rolling suitcase containing men's clothing and a tactical vest with a "security" patch near the crime scene. A Ruger pistol was found on a neighboring property along with a note stating that another person had given Waggle permission to use the firearm for firearm qualifications, according to the affidavit. A judge signed the first-degree murder warrant for Waggle, and he was taken into custody at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office.

hero.headline: Martin County Employee Rescues 3 Girls From Rip Current at Bob Graham Beach
hero.teaser: An off-duty Martin County worker used her surfboard to pull three girls from a rip current at the unguarded Bob Graham Beach near Jensen Beach, then drove one of them to a lifeguard station for medical help.
hero.body:
A Martin County employee helped rescue three girls caught in a rip current Thursday afternoon at Bob Graham Beach near Jensen Beach. Amy Offenbach, who works in the county's Growth and Development Department, said she arrived at the beach around 2 p.m. to surf when she spotted three girls about 25 yards offshore clinging to the same surfboard.

Offenbach, an avid surfer, said something about the scene immediately caught her attention. "The ocean could be very gentle and calm, but it can also be very heavy and crash very hard," she said. She grew concerned when one of the girls appeared distressed. "That kind of struck me as strange," Offenbach said. "The other one seemed a little agitated." A girl on the beach then told Offenbach she believed her friends needed help. "By that time the girls were waving in the water like they needed help, so immediately I just went into rescue mode," Offenbach said.

Offenbach and a friend paddled out to the group. When she reached them, she said one girl appeared to be in serious distress. "I looked at her, and she seemed kind of dazed and confused," Offenbach said. "I said, 'Get up on the board.'" Offenbach gave her surfboard to two of the girls and told them to hold on and kick toward shore, then placed the third girl on her soft-top board and paddled her back to the beach. Offenbach said she has some lifeguard training and quickly recognized the girl needed medical attention. "The girl that I rescued said that she blacked out under the water," Offenbach said. "She inhaled water, and she had a severe headache."

Because Bob Graham Beach is unguarded, Offenbach drove the girl to a nearby lifeguard station, where an ambulance was called. Offenbach said she has not been able to reconnect with the girl or learn more about her condition. She hopes the rescue reminds beachgoers to understand ocean conditions before entering the water, and she encourages people to swim at guarded beaches when possible, check rip current forecasts, and use flotation devices or boards when appropriate. "I'm just really happy that I was in the right place at the right time," Offenbach said. She added that while she loves spending time in the ocean, it can be dangerous. "It can be very treacherous."

cards.headline: MARTY Bus Service Halts Without Warning Across Martin County
cards.body:
MARTY public transit service across Martin County stopped abruptly Thursday, leaving riders who depend on the buses without transportation as county officials work to find a fix. Martin County officials said they received no advance warning that service would stop. The system's operator, Martin County Transit LLC, had requested a significant increase in its contract, saying rising insurance, fuel and maintenance costs had caused significant financial losses since it took over operations in July 2025. Negotiations between the county and the company failed to produce an agreement.

County officials said Martin County Transit LLC submitted a 180-day notice to terminate its contract approximately two weeks ago. Despite that notice, the company told the county Thursday morning that it was discontinuing service immediately, catching officials off guard and cutting off bus routes countywide without notice to riders.

George Stokus, assistant Martin County administrator, said the county is pursuing both short-term and long-term solutions to restore service. "We are doing everything we can humanly do right now to restore service as soon as we can," Stokus said. "It's just not an easy operation or switch to turn it back on. It's going to take some time, and we are working to get to that." County officials said they are coordinating with community partners, including United Way, to help residents affected by the shutdown. No timeline has been given for when MARTY service might resume, and officials said updates will be posted on social media as a solution is reached.

The suspension caught riders by surprise. Leticia Chaclan, of Martin County, waited for her bus in Stuart on Thursday, but it never arrived. She said she had been riding MARTY for years and called it essential for many in the community. "We really need the bus," she said. "Especially people within the Hispanic community, who don't have a driver's license, and need it to go to places like the clinic, to go to the hospital, and for other things we need. It's very necessary, and we use the bus a lot. In my case, I don't drive. But I really need the bus, and I use it a lot. I don't drive, and we go everywhere to shop." Steven Godell, another rider, said he resorted to riding his bicycle Thursday after the bus failed to show. "It's crazy, but I will move on and do something different," he said.

hero.headline: DeSantis Confirms 2 Deaths in Escambia County as Isaias Recovery Continues
hero.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis confirmed Saturday that two people died in Escambia County from causes related to Hurricane Isaias, as more than 430,000 customers across Florida remained without power following the storm's landfall in the Panhandle. Speaking from Destin, DeSantis said the Category 2 hurricane came ashore in Okaloosa County Friday night and caused widespread damage across Northwest Florida, primarily from falling trees and debris.

Escambia County Sheriff Chip Simmons said in videos posted to Facebook that one woman died after a tree fell on her home. A man died after using a generator that was not properly ventilated inside a garage, Simmons said. Four other people inside the same home were hospitalized. "What I saw was both from the structural perspective, I think our structures handled the storm very well," DeSantis said. "The problem is that the storm knocked over a lot of trees."

State emergency crews have completed roughly 180 missions through the Florida Division of Emergency Management, according to DeSantis. Nearly 10,000 power accounts have already been restored, but about 430,000 customers remained without electricity Saturday morning, including roughly 325,000 within Florida Power & Light's service area. Officials said debris removal remains one of the biggest obstacles to restoring power. "The folks have been out since daylight," DeSantis said. "Some of it is that you've got to get the debris out of the way before the linemen can connect it." The Florida Department of Transportation began clearing roads and bridges before sunrise, and the Florida Highway Patrol has completed dozens of debris-clearing missions. State officials said 85 traffic signals have been restored using generators. Northwest Florida Beaches International Airport has reopened to commercial traffic, while airports in Pensacola and Fort Walton Beach remained closed Saturday but were expected to resume operations soon. Florida Division of Emergency Management Executive Director Jared Perdue said more than 16,000 utility workers have been mobilized to restore power in the region.

Perdue warned that flooding risks remain even after the storm has passed, noting that several rivers, including the Shoal River in Okaloosa County, are still rising and are not expected to crest for several days. "We want to make sure we keep enough resources on hand in case search and rescue is needed," Perdue said. State leaders urged residents to avoid flooded roads and standing water. Attorney General James Uthmeier said a small number of price-gouging complaints have already been filed, and residents who believe businesses are overcharging for fuel, food or other emergency supplies can file complaints with his office. Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia warned residents about post-storm scams, including unlicensed contractors and fraudulent roofers, and urged people not to sign contracts or provide deposits before verifying credentials. The state plans to set up insurance assistance hubs in affected areas within 48 hours to help residents file claims. Businesses can report storm damage through the state's survey at FloridaDisaster.biz. DeSantis said recovery efforts will continue across the Panhandle, where damage stretches from the Alabama state line to the eastern Panhandle. "We're going to get through this," DeSantis said. "There's damage, and that's going to be difficult for people whose property was damaged, but I also feel like this is very surmountable for us if we all just work together and get the job done."

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Garage Fire Injures Renter, Community Rallies to Help Family
hero.body:
A fire that tore through the garage of a Port St. Lucie home Friday afternoon injured a father and displaced his family, prompting neighbors and church members to step in and help with cleanup. The fire broke out on Carmelite Street in the Northport Village neighborhood. St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded around 1:30 p.m. and found heavy fire coming from the garage.

According to the family, the fire started in the kitchen before spreading into the garage. They said a propane tank later exploded, causing additional damage and affecting a neighbor's garage doors across the street. When firefighters put out the flames, they left behind a charred garage door, blackened walls and belongings covered in soot.

Renter Nigel Laidlow was inside the home when the fire started and suffered burns to his legs. He was transported for medical treatment. "I don't even know how to describe it. It was really surreal," Laidlow said. "I would've never thought a little fire would turn into this."

By Saturday, family photos, furniture and other belongings were spread across the front yard as loved ones worked to salvage what they could. Members of the Fort Pierce Seventh-day Adventist Church spent the day helping move and sort through the damaged items. "We have a really strong support system, especially from my church," Laidlow said. Despite the loss, he said he is grateful his family survived. "This right here is something not anybody would like to deal with. Not in a lifetime," he said. The family is now focused on recovering and figuring out its next steps, and the cause of the fire remains under investigation.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Launches Flood Sensors as California/Savona Fix Looms
cards.teaser: After flooding shut down a pizza shop and turned the intersection into what neighbors call the "California River," Port St. Lucie is rolling out water-level sensors while a larger drainage project remains years away.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie is starting a pilot program using water-level sensors at flood-prone areas, including the intersection of California and Savona boulevards, after this week's flooding forced a nearby pizza shop to close early and cost it thousands of dollars in lost revenue. The water at the intersection has receded, but earlier this week the roadway looked like a lake.

Joe Dascoli, who works at Estella Pizzaria near the intersection, said the flooding has become a recurring problem. "We were actually calling it the California River, as a joke," Dascoli said. "It becomes like an island around here." That island is the shopping plaza where the pizza shop sits. Dascoli said customers could not get in and orders could not get out during this week's flooding, and some delivery drivers could not get their cars through the water. "We've lost thousands of dollars just in revenue and people not being able to come in," Dascoli said. "It's an ongoing thing that you know should be resolved."

Scott Samples with the city of Port St. Lucie said the new sensor pilot program will send alerts to Public Works and police when an area starts seeing rapid flooding, allowing crews to respond faster. The sensors are meant to address immediate flooding risks while the city works on a longer-term solution.

That long-term fix is a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes building two new retention ponds, installing baffle boxes to collect runoff, and raising sections of roadway at California and Savona boulevards. Samples said the project is currently in the data collection phase and has not yet moved into design. "This is one of the highest priorities that we have in terms of capital investment projects, and so it's going to take time," Samples said.

hero.headline: Martin County Employee Pulls Drowning Girl From Water at Unguarded Stuart Beach
hero.teaser: Amy Offenbach grabbed a surfboard and paddled out to rescue a choking, limp girl at Bob Graham Beach, which had no lifeguards on duty at the time.
hero.body:
A Martin County employee is being praised for rescuing a girl from drowning Thursday afternoon at Bob Graham Beach in Stuart, where no lifeguards were on duty. Amy Offenbach had come to the beach to surf when she saw three girls struggling in the water. "It was just by chance that we were here and thank God that we were at the right time," Offenbach said.

Offenbach, who has years of lifeguard training, said her instincts took over immediately. "I took off my clothes, grabbed the board, and started paddling," she said. "I immediately went into rescue mode." Authorities said one of the girls was choking on water. Offenbach used her surfboard to stabilize the child as she brought her out of the water.

"Once she was on the board, she was kind of limp. Her body wasn't doing anything else," Offenbach said. She said the girl's forehead felt cold, which prompted her to rush the child to the nearest lifeguard stand down the road. The girl was then taken to the hospital with minor drowning injuries.

Offenbach, a Martin County employee, said she does not feel the need for recognition, even as others have called her a hero. She said she was simply acting on instinct as a mother. "I have a 14-year-old son myself, and I can't imagine him not coming back from hanging out at the beach with his friends," she said. "I'm just really thankful that her parents have their child," Offenbach said. The incident is a reminder to use caution at beaches that do not have lifeguards on duty.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast High Freshman Dies After Being Struck on Port St. Lucie Boulevard
hero.body:
A 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student has died after being struck by a vehicle while walking to school in Port St. Lucie on Wednesday morning. The Port St. Lucie Police Department confirmed the death in a news release issued at 8 p.m. Friday, three days after the crash near the intersection of Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard and Southwest Squirrel Avenue.

Chief Leo Niemczyk announced the student's death in a statement headlined "14-YEAR-OLD PEDESTRIAN SUCCUMBS TO INJURIES FOLLOWING CRASH." "The Port St. Lucie Police Department extends its deepest condolences to the student's family, friends, classmates, and all those affected by this heartbreaking loss. Our thoughts are with them during this incredibly difficult time," the department said.

Police said a preliminary investigation found the freshman was walking northbound along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near the edge of the roadway when he was struck from behind by a 2002 Ford Excursion driven by a 72-year-old man. According to investigators, the driver initially believed he had hit a construction barrel and did not realize he had struck a person. The driver later made a U-turn at the next safe location, returned to the scene, turned on his hazard lights and found the teenager unconscious on the side of the road.

Police said the driver has remained cooperative with investigators and that they have not observed any signs of impairment. Authorities stressed that the assessment is preliminary and could change as the investigation continues. Detectives are still examining the circumstances surrounding the crash.

cards.headline: Church, Neighbors Help Port St. Lucie Family After Carmelite Street House Fire
cards.teaser: A fire that spread through a Port St. Lucie garage and triggered a propane tank explosion injured a renter and displaced his family. Church members and neighbors spent Saturday helping them salvage belongings.
cards.body:
A fire that spread through the garage of a Port St. Lucie home Friday afternoon injured a renter and displaced his family, prompting neighbors and church members to help them begin cleaning up. The fire broke out on Carmelite Street in the Northport Village neighborhood. According to the family, it started in the kitchen before spreading into the garage, where a propane tank later exploded, causing additional damage and damaging a neighbor's garage doors across the street.

St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded to the home around 1:30 p.m. Friday and found heavy fire coming from the garage. After firefighters put out the flames, the home was left with a charred garage door, blackened walls and belongings covered in soot. Renter Nigel Laidlow was inside when the fire started and suffered burns to his legs. He was transported for medical treatment.

"I don't even know how to describe it. It was really surreal," Laidlow said. "I would've never thought a little fire would turn into this."

By Saturday, family photos, furniture and other belongings were spread across the front yard as loved ones worked to salvage what they could. Members of the Fort Pierce Seventh-day Adventist Church spent the day helping move and sort through the damaged items. "We have a really strong support system, especially from my church," Laidlow said. Despite the loss, he said he is grateful his family survived. "This right here is something not anybody would like to deal with. Not in a lifetime," he said. The family is now focused on recovering and determining its next steps, and the cause of the fire remains under investigation.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Flooding at California, Savona Boulevards Costs Pizza Shop Thousands
cards.teaser: Repeated flooding at the Port St. Lucie intersection of California and Savona boulevards has forced Estella Pizzaria to close early and halt deliveries, and the city says a permanent fix will take time.
cards.body:
Flooding this week at the intersection of California and Savona boulevards in Port St. Lucie turned the roadway into what neighbors jokingly called the "California River," and it hit the nearby Estella Pizzaria hard enough to force an early closure. The water has since receded, but the shop says it has already lost thousands of dollars in revenue because of the recurring problem.

Joe Dascoli, who works at Estella Pizzaria, said the shopping plaza where the restaurant sits becomes "like an island" whenever the intersection floods. Because of the flooding on Thursday, the shop had to close early. Dascoli said customers could not get in and orders could not get out during the latest flooding, and some delivery drivers could not get their cars through the water, forcing the shop to stop deliveries altogether.

"We've lost thousands of dollars just in revenue and people not being able to come in," Dascoli said. "Some of our drivers, their cars aren't capable of going through the floods, so we have to stop deliveries." He added that the flooding is "an ongoing thing that you know should be resolved."

The city of Port St. Lucie is rolling out a pilot program that installs water level sensors in flood-prone areas, according to Scott Samples with the city. Samples said the sensors will send alerts to Public Works and police when an area is seeing rapid flooding so crews can respond more quickly. For a long-term solution, the city is planning a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood that includes two new retention ponds, baffle boxes to collect runoff, and raising sections of the roadway at California and Savona boulevards. Samples said the project is currently in the data collection phase before design work begins. "This is one of the highest priorities that we have in terms of capital investment projects, and so it's going to take time," Samples said.

hero.headline: Nearly 450,000 Without Power in Florida After Hurricane Isaias, No Confirmed Deaths Yet
hero.body:
Nearly 450,000 utility customers remained without power across Northwest Florida on Saturday morning after Hurricane Isaias made landfall in the Panhandle, and state officials said no storm-related fatalities had been confirmed as recovery efforts continued. Gov. Ron DeSantis delivered the update during a statewide briefing, saying the storm came ashore near Destin at 9:30 p.m. Friday as a Category 2 hurricane with sustained winds of about 105 mph. Wind gusts reached as high as 116 mph near Santa Rosa Sound, and storm surge pushed water levels about 5.5 feet above normal in some areas.

DeSantis said there have been no confirmed fatalities, though state officials are still looking into a possible death in Escambia County linked to a fallen tree. The storm has since weakened into a post-tropical cyclone and moved out of Florida, but DeSantis warned that flooding remains a concern, particularly in parts of the Panhandle and Big Bend, where 4 to 8 inches of rain are expected through the weekend.

More than 16,000 linemen were staged ahead of the storm and began restoration work as early as 3 a.m. Saturday. By 7 a.m., about 448,000 customer accounts were without electricity statewide, including roughly 323,000 Florida Power & Light customers and about 110,000 customers served by electric cooperatives. Santa Rosa County was among the hardest hit, with about 90% of customers without power, followed by Holmes County at 89%, Washington County at 86%, Walton County at 85%, Escambia County at 75% and Okaloosa County at 53%. The Florida Department of Transportation and Florida Highway Patrol ran overnight "cut and toss" operations to clear roads of fallen trees and debris, and officials said all state-owned bridges had been inspected and reopened by 6 a.m. Northwest Florida Beaches International Airport resumed commercial operations Saturday morning, while Destin-Fort Walton Beach Airport and Pensacola International Airport remained closed.

cards.headline: Red Cross Aids Port St. Lucie Family After Northwest Carmelite Street Fire
cards.teaser: Four people, including two children, received emergency assistance after a house fire on Northwest Carmelite Street in Port St. Lucie. Red Cross volunteers also helped a Riviera Beach fire victim the same day.
cards.body:
The American Red Cross assisted four people, including two adults and two children, after a house fire at a home on Northwest Carmelite Street in Port St. Lucie. The organization's Disaster Action Team volunteers responded to the fire as part of a news release issued Friday, Oct. 9, which detailed assistance provided to a total of five people displaced by two separate house fires within a 12-hour period.

The second fire struck a home on West 28th Street in Riviera Beach, where one adult received help from Red Cross volunteers. The Red Cross did not release information about what caused either fire or the extent of the damage at either location.

Red Cross Disaster Action Team volunteers are specially trained to respond to emergencies 24 hours a day, seven days a week. For the family displaced from the Northwest Carmelite Street home, volunteers provided emergency financial assistance, health and mental health services, and recovery support. All Red Cross disaster assistance is provided free of charge and funded through donations.

Residents who want to support disaster relief efforts for families like the one displaced in Port St. Lucie can donate at redcross.org/donate. The Red Cross also offers information about home fire safety and preparedness at redcross.org/homefires, resources aimed at helping Treasure Coast residents reduce their risk of displacement from future house fires.

hero.headline: MARTY Bus Service Halted Without Warning Across Martin County
hero.body:
MARTY public transit service in Martin County came to an abrupt halt Thursday, leaving riders who depend on the system without their regular transportation while county officials scramble for a fix. Martin County officials said they received no advance warning that service would stop that day.

According to the county, MARTY's operator, Martin County Transit LLC, had requested a significant increase in its contract. The company says rising insurance, fuel and maintenance costs have caused significant financial losses since it began running the service in July 2025. Negotiations between the county and the operator failed to produce an agreement. County officials said the company gave 180 days' notice to terminate its contract about two weeks ago, but then notified the county Thursday morning that it was immediately discontinuing service.

George Stokus, assistant Martin County administrator, said officials are exploring both short-term and long-term solutions to restore service. "We are doing everything we can humanly do right now to restore service as soon as we can," Stokus said. "It's just not an easy operation or switch to turn it back on. It's going to take some time, and we are working to get to that." County officials said they are working with community partners, including United Way, to help residents affected by the shutdown. No timeline has been set for when MARTY operations will resume, and officials said they will post updates on social media and notify residents once a solution is reached.

The sudden suspension left riders stranded across Martin County. Leticia Chaclan waited for a bus in Stuart on Thursday that never came, and said she was unaware the service had been suspended until a reporter told her. Chaclan said she has ridden the bus for years and called it essential for many in the community. "We really need the bus," she said. "Especially people within the Hispanic community, who don't have a driver's license, and need it to go to places like the clinic, to go to the hospital, and for other things we need. It's very necessary, and we use the bus a lot. In my case, I don't drive. But I really need the bus, and I use it a lot. I don't drive, and we go everywhere to shop." Steven Godell, another rider affected by the shutdown, said he was on his bicycle Thursday after the MARTY bus did not show up that morning. "It's crazy, but I will move on and do something different," he said.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Man Arrested on Murder Charge in August Shooting Death of Ex-Girlfriend
hero.body:
A 33-year-old Vero Beach man is being held without bond after his Oct. 5 arrest on a first-degree murder warrant in the August shooting death of his former girlfriend, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Matthew Allen Waggle was taken into custody at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office on the warrant, which accuses him of killing Dawn Marie Kriskewic. A judge had signed the warrant in August.

Deputies were called to the 500 block of 1st Street after 911 callers reported a woman lying in the roadway. They found Kriskewic with injuries consistent with gunshot wounds and began CPR before she was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she was pronounced dead. Investigators identified Waggle as Kriskewic's former boyfriend.

According to the arrest affidavit, a coworker told detectives that Kriskewic had expressed concerns about Waggle before her death. The coworker also said Waggle had previously threatened consequences if Kriskewic called police when he came to retrieve his belongings. Surveillance footage reviewed by detectives showed a person they identified as Waggle in the area around the time of the shooting, as well as walking through the area before and after it. That footage also showed him discarding a shirt, which investigators later recovered.

Investigators recovered a rolling suitcase containing men's clothing and a tactical vest with a "security" patch near the crime scene. A Ruger pistol was found on a neighboring property along with a note stating that another person had given Waggle permission to use the firearm for firearm qualifications, according to the affidavit. Waggle remains held without bond at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office on the first-degree murder charge.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Rolls Out Flood Sensors After California Boulevard Flooding Hurts Business
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie is launching a pilot program to install water level sensors at flood-prone intersections after recent flooding at California and Savona boulevards cost a nearby pizza shop thousands of dollars in lost business. The intersection flooded badly earlier this week, with standing water covering the roadway like a lake before receding.

Joe Dascoli, who works at Estella Pizzaria near the intersection, said the flooding turns the surrounding shopping plaza into an island. "We were actually calling it the California River, as a joke," Dascoli said. "It becomes like an island around here." The shop had to close early on Thursday because of the flooding, and Dascoli said customers could not get in and orders could not go out. "We've lost thousands of dollars just in revenue and people not being able to come in," Dascoli said. "Some of our drivers, their cars aren't capable of going through the floods, so we have to stop deliveries."

City officials say they are responding with both immediate and long-term measures. Scott Samples with the city of Port St. Lucie said the new pilot program will place water level sensors in flood-prone areas to alert Public Works and police when rapid flooding begins. "There'll be alerts that'll be able to go to Public Works and the police to say, 'Hey, this area is seeing rapid flooding,' so they might be able to respond quicker," Samples said.

For a longer-term fix, Samples pointed to a large-scale drainage project planned for the Oak Hammock neighborhood. The project calls for two new retention ponds, baffle boxes to collect runoff, and raised sections of roadway at California and Savona boulevards. Samples said the project is currently in the data collection phase and has not yet moved into design. "This is one of the highest priorities that we have in terms of capital investment projects, and so it's going to take time," Samples said. Dascoli said the flooding is "an ongoing thing that you know should be resolved."

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Teen Dies After Being Struck Walking to School on PSL Boulevard
hero.body:
A 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student has died after being struck by a vehicle while walking to school in Port St. Lucie. The Port St. Lucie Police Department said the crash happened near the intersection of SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard and SW Squirrel Avenue on the morning of Oct. 8.

A preliminary investigation found the teen was walking northbound along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near the edge of the roadway when he was struck from behind by a 2002 Ford Excursion driven by a 72-year-old man. Detectives are continuing to examine the circumstances surrounding the crash, and the investigation remains active.

The Port St. Lucie Police Department extended its condolences to the student's family, friends and classmates, saying in a statement that its thoughts are with them during this difficult time.

cards.headline: Grease Fire Sparks Propane Explosion at Port St. Lucie Home
cards.teaser: A grease fire in a garage touched off a propane tank explosion that hurled debris across a Port St. Lucie street Friday afternoon, destroying most of a family's belongings and briefly sending the father to the hospital.
cards.body:
A grease fire inside the garage of a Port St. Lucie home ignited a propane tank explosion Friday afternoon that destroyed nearly everything a family of four owned. St. Lucie County Fire District received the initial call at 1:24 p.m. for a fire at a home in the 100 block of Carmelite Street after neighbors spotted smoke and called 911.

Neighbors said the man who lives at the home told them he had been cooking when a grease fire broke out in the garage, where a propane tank was stored. The blast launched the tank out of the garage, across the street, and into a neighbor's garage. Marina Cheong, who lives a few doors down, said she was in her backyard when she saw heavy smoke and ran toward the home to help, only to be stopped by the explosion. "And then there was explosion, very loud, loud explosion, and debris started flying everywhere," she said.

Neighbor Rob Roadman said he heard the blast before he saw what caused it. "I heard a huge explosion. At first, I thought maybe it's a transformer or something, but it was much, much, much louder than that," he said. "I thought it was an air raid. It was not a casual thing. My house shook," he added. Cheong described a similar reaction, saying, "I thought that the whole house had exploded. It was very loud." Roadman said he checked on the father shortly afterward. "I asked the dad if he was OK, and he goes, 'Yeah.' But you could tell he wasn't. Who wouldn't be?" Roadman said.

The father was briefly hospitalized but returned to the home a few hours later to join family and friends sifting through the wreckage. They found little worth saving. A family member said they consider themselves lucky that no one was seriously injured and credited a strong community and church for helping them through the aftermath.

cards.headline: Church Members Help Port St. Lucie Family After Carmelite Street House Fire
cards.teaser: A renter suffered leg burns escaping a fire that tore through his Port St. Lucie home, and members of a Fort Pierce church are now helping the displaced family clean up.
cards.body:
A fire tore through the garage of a home on Carmelite Street in Port St. Lucie's Northport Village neighborhood Friday afternoon, injuring a man and displacing his family. St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded around 1:30 p.m. and arrived to find heavy fire coming from the garage. According to the family, the fire started in the kitchen before spreading through the garage, and a propane tank later exploded, causing additional damage and impacting a neighbor's garage doors across the street.

Renter Nigel Laidlow was inside the home when the fire broke out and suffered burns to his legs. He was transported for medical treatment. "I don't even know how to describe it. It was really surreal," Laidlow said. "I would've never thought a little fire would turn into this."

Firefighters extinguished the flames, but significant damage was left behind, including a charred garage door, blackened walls and belongings covered in soot. By Saturday, family photos, furniture and other belongings were spread across the front yard as loved ones worked to salvage what they could. Members of the Fort Pierce Seventh-day Adventist Church spent the day helping move and sort through the damaged items. "We have a really strong support system, especially from my church," Laidlow said.

Despite the loss, Laidlow said he is grateful his family survived. "This right here is something not anybody would like to deal with. Not in a lifetime," he said. The family is now focused on recovering and determining its next steps, and the cause of the fire remains under investigation.

"Some of our drivers, their cars aren't capable of going through the floods, so we have to stop deliveries."

The city of Port St. Lucie confirmed the flooding problem and outlined steps it is taking to address it. Scott Samples with the city said Port St. Lucie is starting a pilot program that will install water level sensors at flood-prone areas around the city. "There'll be alerts that'll be able to go to Public Works and the police to say, 'Hey, this area is seeing rapid flooding,' so they might be able to respond quicker," Samples said.

Samples said a long-term fix will involve a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood. The project calls for two new retention ponds, baffle boxes to collect runoff, and raising sections of the roadway at California and Savona boulevards. The project is currently in the data collection phase before moving into design. "This is one of the highest priorities that we have in terms of capital investment projects, and so it's going to take time," Samples said.

hero.headline: Martin County Employee Rescues Three Girls From Rip Current at Bob Graham Beach
hero.teaser: A county worker with lifeguard training pulled three girls from a rip current at the unguarded Jensen Beach access point, then drove one girl showing signs of distress to a nearby lifeguard station for help.
hero.body:
A Martin County employee helped rescue three girls caught in a rip current Thursday afternoon at Bob Graham Beach in Jensen Beach, an unguarded stretch of shoreline. Amy Offenbach, who works in Martin County's Growth and Development Department and is an avid surfer, said she arrived at the beach around 2 p.m. to surf when she noticed three girls about 25 yards offshore holding onto the same surfboard.

Offenbach said something about the scene caught her attention right away. "The ocean could be very gentle and calm, but it can also be very heavy and crash very hard," she said. She grew concerned when one of the girls appeared distressed. "That kind of struck me as strange," Offenbach said. "The other one seemed a little agitated." Moments later, a girl on the beach told Offenbach she believed her friends needed help. "By that time the girls were waving in the water like they needed help, so immediately I just went into rescue mode," Offenbach said.

Offenbach and a friend paddled out to the girls. When she reached the group, she said one girl appeared to be in serious distress. "I looked at her, and she seemed kind of dazed and confused," Offenbach said. "I said, 'Get up on the board.'" Offenbach gave her surfboard to two of the girls and told them to hold on and kick toward shore, then placed the third girl on her soft-top board and paddled her back to the beach. Offenbach, who has some lifeguard training, quickly recognized the girl needed medical attention. "The girl that I rescued said that she blacked out under the water," Offenbach said. "She inhaled water, and she had a severe headache." Because Bob Graham Beach has no lifeguard on duty, Offenbach drove the girl to a nearby lifeguard station, where an ambulance was called.

Offenbach said she hopes the rescue reminds beachgoers to understand ocean conditions before entering the water. She encourages people to swim at guarded beaches when possible, check rip current forecasts, and use flotation devices or boards when appropriate. "I'm just really happy that I was in the right place at the right time," she said. Offenbach said she has not been able to reconnect with the girl she rescued or learn more about her condition. "It can be very treacherous," Offenbach said of the ocean. "Treacherous."

cards.headline: Martin County Scrambles to Restore MARTY Bus Service After Sudden Shutdown
cards.body:
Martin County's public transit system, MARTY, abruptly stopped running Thursday, leaving riders who depend on it for medical appointments, work and shopping trips without transportation. County officials said they received no advance warning before the service halted.

MARTY's operator, Martin County Transit LLC, had asked the county for a significant increase in its contract, citing rising insurance, fuel and maintenance costs that the company says have caused significant financial losses since it took over the service in July 2025. Negotiations between the county and the company failed to produce an agreement. County officials said the company gave formal notice about two weeks ago that it would terminate its contract in 180 days, but then notified the county Thursday morning that it was ending service immediately.

George Stokus, assistant Martin County administrator, said the county is pursuing both short-term and long-term fixes to get buses running again. "We are doing everything we can humanly do right now to restore service as soon as we can," Stokus said. "It's just not an easy operation or switch to turn it back on. It's going to take some time, and we are working to get to that." The county has not given a timeline for when service will resume and says it will post updates on social media as a solution develops. Officials said they are also working with community partners, including United Way, to help residents affected by the shutdown.

The sudden halt caught riders off guard. Leticia Chaclan of Martin County waited for a bus in Stuart on Thursday that never arrived, and said she had been unaware the service was suspended until a reporter told her. Chaclan said she has ridden MARTY for years and called it essential for many in the community, especially those without a driver's license. "We really need the bus," she said. "Especially people within the Hispanic community, who don't have a driver's license, and need it to go to places like the clinic, to go to the hospital, and for other things we need. It's very necessary, and we use the bus a lot. In my case, I don't drive. But I really need the bus, and I use it a lot. I don't drive, and we go everywhere to shop." Rider Steven Godell said he rode his bicycle Thursday after the bus failed to show up that morning. "It's crazy, but I will move on and do something different," he said.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Man Arrested on Murder Charge in Girlfriend's Shooting Death
cards.body:
A 33-year-old Vero Beach man is being held without bond on a first-degree murder charge in connection with the August shooting death of his former girlfriend, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Matthew Allen Waggle was arrested Oct. 5 on an active warrant accusing him of killing Dawn Marie Kriskewic. He was taken into custody at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office.

Deputies were called to the 500 block of 1st Street in August after 911 callers reported a woman lying in the roadway. They found Kriskewic with injuries consistent with gunshot wounds and began CPR before she was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.

Investigators identified Waggle as Kriskewic's former boyfriend. A coworker told detectives that Kriskewic had expressed concerns about him before her death and said Waggle had previously threatened consequences if Kriskewic called police when he came to retrieve his belongings. Detectives said surveillance footage showed a person they identified as Waggle near the scene around the time of the shooting, and additional footage showed him walking through the area both before and after the shooting. That footage also showed him discarding a shirt, which investigators later recovered.

Near the crime scene, investigators found a rolling suitcase containing men's clothing and a tactical vest with a "security" patch. A Ruger pistol was recovered on a neighboring property along with a note stating that another person had given Waggle permission to use the firearm for firearm qualifications, according to the arrest affidavit. A judge signed the first-degree murder warrant for Waggle in August, and he remains held without bond following his October arrest.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Flooding at California, Savona Boulevards Costs Pizza Shop Thousands
cards.teaser: Chronic flooding at the Port St. Lucie intersection of California and Savona boulevards forced Estella Pizzaria to close early this week, and city officials say a lasting fix is still years away.
cards.body:
Flooding at the intersection of California and Savona boulevards in Port St. Lucie has cost a nearby pizza shop thousands of dollars in lost revenue, and city officials say a permanent solution is still in the early planning stages. Floodwaters receded this week after turning the intersection into what looked like a lake earlier in the week.

Joe Dascoli, who works at Estella Pizzaria near the intersection, said the shopping plaza where the restaurant sits becomes isolated during heavy flooding. "We were actually calling it the California River, as a joke," Dascoli said. "It becomes like an island around here." The flooding forced the shop to close early on Thursday, cutting off customers and delivery drivers alike. "We've lost thousands of dollars just in revenue and people not being able to come in," Dascoli said. "Some of our drivers, their cars aren't capable of going through the floods, so we have to stop deliveries."

City officials said they are rolling out a pilot program to install water level sensors at flood-prone locations around Port St. Lucie. Scott Samples, speaking for the city, said the sensors would send alerts to Public Works and police when an area starts flooding rapidly, allowing crews to respond faster. The sensor program is aimed at addressing immediate response times rather than the underlying drainage problem.

A longer-term fix is planned for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, where the city intends to build two new retention ponds and install baffle boxes to capture runoff. The project also calls for raising sections of the roadway at California and Savona boulevards. Samples said the project is currently in the data collection phase and has not yet moved into design. "This is one of the highest priorities that we have in terms of capital investment projects, and so it's going to take time," Samples said.

hero.headline: MARTY Bus Service Halts Abruptly in Martin County, No Restart Date Set
hero.body:
MARTY public transit service in Martin County came to an abrupt halt Thursday, leaving riders who depend on the bus system without regular transportation while county officials scramble for a solution. Martin County officials said they were given no advance warning that service would stop. MARTY's operator, Martin County Transit LLC, had requested a significant increase in its contract with the county, saying rising insurance, fuel and maintenance costs had caused significant financial losses since it took over the service in July 2025. Negotiations between the county and the company failed to produce an agreement.

County officials said Martin County Transit LLC gave formal notice about two weeks ago that it would terminate its contract in 180 days. But Thursday morning, the company told the county it was discontinuing service immediately, with no transition period. George Stokus, assistant Martin County administrator, said the county is now working on both short-term and long-term fixes to get buses running again. "We are doing everything we can humanly do right now to restore service as soon as we can," Stokus said. "It's just not an easy operation or switch to turn it back on. It's going to take some time, and we are working to get to that."

County officials said they are coordinating with community partners, including United Way, to help residents affected by the shutdown. No timeline has been set for when MARTY service will resume, and officials said they will post updates on social media and notify residents once a solution is reached.

The sudden loss of service caught riders off guard. Leticia Chaclan, of Martin County, waited for a bus in Stuart on Thursday that never came. She said she did not know MARTY had been suspended until a reporter told her. Chaclan said she has ridden the bus for years and called it essential for many in the community, especially Hispanic residents without driver's licenses who rely on it to reach clinics, hospitals and stores. "We really need the bus," she said. "Especially people within the Hispanic community, who don't have a driver's license, and need it to go to places like the clinic, to go to the hospital, and for other things we need. It's very necessary, and we use the bus a lot. In my case, I don't drive. But I really need the bus, and I use it a lot. I don't drive, and we go everywhere to shop." Steven Godell, another rider affected by the shutdown, said he rode his bicycle Thursday after the bus failed to show up that morning. "It's crazy, but I will move on and do something different," he said.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Teen Hit Walking to School Remains Critical, No Charges Yet
cards.teaser: A 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student remains in critical condition after being struck from behind near a construction zone on Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard. The driver, a 72-year-old man, stopped and returned to the scene after realizing he had hit a person rather than a construction barrel.
cards.body:
A 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student remains in critical condition after being struck by a vehicle while walking to school Wednesday morning, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. No charges have been filed as the investigation continues.

Police said the crash happened around 6 a.m. near the intersection of Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard and Southwest Squirrel Avenue. The student was walking northbound along Port St. Lucie Boulevard, near the edge of the roadway in an area marked by construction barrels, when he was struck from behind.

Investigators said the vehicle involved was a 2002 Ford Excursion driven by a 72-year-old man. Police said the driver initially believed he had struck a construction barrel and did not realize he had hit a person. He later made a U-turn at the next safe location, returned to the scene, activated his hazard lights and found the teenager unconscious on the side of the roadway.

The driver has remained cooperative with investigators, and police said they have not observed any apparent signs of impairment, though officials noted that assessment is preliminary and could change as the investigation continues. The student, identified only as a freshman at Treasure Coast High School, suffered life-threatening injuries. Anyone who witnessed the crash or has dash-camera, surveillance or other video footage from the area around the time of the incident is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Rolls Out Flood Sensors as California-Savona Drainage Fix Awaits
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie is launching a pilot program using water level sensors at flood-prone spots around the city after repeated flooding at the intersection of California and Savona boulevards cost a nearby pizza shop thousands of dollars in lost business. The flooding turned the intersection into what looked like a lake earlier this week, with the water receding only in recent days.

Joe Dascoli, who works at Estella Pizzaria near the intersection, said the shopping plaza where the restaurant sits becomes isolated during heavy rain. "We were actually calling it the California River, as a joke," Dascoli said. "It becomes like an island around here." The shop had to close early on Thursday because of the flooding, and Dascoli said customers could not get in and delivery orders could not get out. "We've lost thousands of dollars just in revenue and people not being able to come in," he said. "Some of our drivers, their cars aren't capable of going through the floods, so we have to stop deliveries."

City representative Scott Samples said Port St. Lucie is starting the sensor pilot program to monitor flood-prone areas in real time. "There'll be alerts that'll be able to go to Public Works and the police to say, 'Hey, this area is seeing rapid flooding,' so they might be able to respond quicker," Samples said. The sensors would give city crews earlier warning so they can respond to flash flooding before it worsens.

Samples said the long-term solution for the California and Savona corridor is a large-scale drainage project planned for the Oak Hammock neighborhood. The project calls for two new retention ponds, baffle boxes to collect stormwater runoff, and raised sections of roadway at the California and Savona intersection. The project is currently in its data collection phase and has not yet moved into design. "This is one of the highest priorities that we have in terms of capital investment projects, and so it's going to take time," Samples said. Until the Oak Hammock project advances, businesses like Estella Pizzaria remain vulnerable to the kind of flash flooding that shut them down this week.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Search for Driver Who Critically Injured Man in Hit-and-Run
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police are searching for a driver who struck a 63-year-old man and left him critically injured early Friday morning, then fled the scene. The man, a Port St. Lucie resident, was found unconscious in the roadway near the intersection of NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard at about 12:56 a.m.

Police said the victim was suffering from severe head trauma and significant bleeding when he was found. He was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for treatment and remains in critical condition.

Detectives have obtained surveillance video from a nearby business that captured the incident and are continuing to collect and review additional footage as they work to identify the vehicle and driver involved. Investigators have not said whether a description of the vehicle has been developed.

Police are asking anyone who was driving in the area around the time of the crash, anyone who witnessed the incident, or anyone with dashcam or other video footage to come forward. Authorities said even information that may seem insignificant could help investigators identify the driver and resolve the case. Anyone with information is asked to call the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000. The investigation remains active and ongoing.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Man Charged With Murder in August Shooting Death of Ex-Girlfriend
cards.teaser: Matthew Allen Waggle was arrested on a first-degree murder warrant in the shooting death of Dawn Marie Kriskewic, who was found in the roadway on 1st Street in Vero Beach. Surveillance footage and items recovered near the scene led investigators to the charge.
cards.body:
A 33-year-old Vero Beach man has been arrested on a first-degree murder charge in the August shooting death of Dawn Marie Kriskewic, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Matthew Allen Waggle was arrested Oct. 5 on an active warrant and is being held without bond.

Deputies responded to the 500 block of 1st Street after 911 callers reported a woman lying in the roadway. They found Kriskewic with injuries consistent with gunshot wounds and began CPR before she was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.

Investigators identified Waggle as Kriskewic's former boyfriend. A coworker told detectives that Kriskewic had expressed concerns about Waggle before her death and said Waggle had previously threatened consequences if Kriskewic called police when he came to retrieve his belongings. Detectives said surveillance footage showed a person they identified as Waggle near the area around the time of the shooting, and additional footage showed him walking through the area both before and after the shooting. Investigators said the footage also showed him discarding a shirt, which they later recovered.

Near the crime scene, investigators recovered a rolling suitcase containing men's clothing and a tactical vest bearing a "security" patch. A Ruger pistol was found on a neighboring property along with a note stating that another person had given Waggle permission to use the firearm for firearm qualifications, according to the affidavit. A judge signed the first-degree murder warrant for Waggle on Aug. He was taken into custody at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie approves assisted-living site plan despite contamination concerns
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the major site plan for a 150-unit assisted-living facility near a petroleum-contaminated property, even as residents cite an engineering letter showing cleanup plans had to be revised because of the project. The development still needs further agency review before construction can begin.
cards.body:
Sandpiper Bay residents who had asked Port St. Lucie and St. Lucie County fire officials to intervene in a proposed assisted-living development next to a known petroleum-contaminated property are now reacting to news that the city has approved the project's major site plan. The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the major site plan for the facility, known as PSL Westmoreland ALF, in September, despite ongoing objections from nearby residents about the environmental history of the neighboring contaminated property.

The proposed facility is a three-story, 150-unit assisted-living project with a memory care component, planned for 7.1 acres within the Rivella planned unit development along Southeast Morningside Boulevard near Southeast Westmoreland Boulevard. Construction has not begun. The developer must still submit construction plans for technical review, followed by additional agency reviews, including one from the South Florida Water Management District, before building can start.

Residents' concerns center on an engineering letter that provides new detail about the contamination issue. The letter, from BTEX Engineering, discussed a March 2026 meeting with environmental officials about the neighboring property and said the proposed remediation approach should be changed because of concerns about surrounding properties, including the planned assisted-living facility. The letter said vapors would need to be captured during the remediation process.

Resident David Lipps said the issue is not about what is being built on the site, arguing that nearby businesses and other facilities could also be affected by environmental concerns. Resident Charlie D'Agata said residents have raised objections at City Council meetings for about two years and questioned why a developer would be allowed to build near a property he described as contaminated. Residents say they have contacted the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the Florida Department of Health in an effort to get answers about the site.

The environmental history of the neighboring property and the extent of any potential impact on surrounding land remain central questions for residents seeking more information. With the major site plan now approved, residents say they want clearer answers about the contamination and how any risks would be addressed as the project advances through the remaining review steps.

cards.headline: 2 Arrested After Woman Shot At While Fleeing Fort Pierce Attack
cards.teaser: A woman escaped an attack on South Sixth Street and was shot at as she drove away. Fort Pierce police have arrested 18-year-olds Keibin Lopez-Godoy and Kailee Yurubi in connection with the shooting.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police have arrested two 18-year-olds in connection with an attack and shooting that sent a woman fleeing for her life on South Sixth Street earlier this month. Keibin Lopez-Godoy faces a charge of first-degree attempted homicide, and Kailee Yurubi faces a charge of accessory after the fact.

The case began on Saturday, October 3, when Fort Pierce police officers responded to South Sixth Street at 7:12 a.m. after the victim called 911 to report that someone was shooting at her. Investigators said the woman had gone to the address to speak with her boyfriend about their relationship. When she arrived, several people ran out of the residence and began attacking her, according to police.

The victim managed to break free, get into her vehicle, and drive away from the scene, police said. As she fled, one of the suspects grabbed a gun from the property and opened fire on her vehicle, according to investigators.

Police said a second person was arrested for allegedly driving the shooter away from the scene after the attack. Lopez-Godoy and Yurubi were both identified as the suspects taken into custody in the case.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Seek Driver Who Struck Man on NW University Boulevard
hero.teaser: A 63-year-old man remains in critical condition after a hit-and-run crash early Friday near NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard. Detectives have surveillance video of the crash but are still searching for the driver and vehicle involved.
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police are searching for a driver who struck a 63-year-old man early Friday morning and left him critically injured in the roadway. The crash happened around 12:56 a.m. near the intersection of NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard, and the driver did not stay at the scene.

The victim, a Port St. Lucie resident, was found unconscious with severe head trauma and significant bleeding, police said. He was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where he remains in critical condition.

Detectives have obtained surveillance video from a nearby business that captured the incident and are continuing to collect and review additional footage from the area. Investigators are working to determine exactly how the crash happened and to identify the vehicle and driver involved.

Police are asking anyone who was driving in the area around the time of the crash, witnessed the incident, or has dashcam or other video footage to come forward. Officials said even small details could help investigators identify the driver and move the case toward resolution. Anyone with information is asked to call the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000. The investigation remains active.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Man Arrested on Murder Warrant in Girlfriend's Shooting Death
cards.body:
A 33-year-old Vero Beach man has been arrested on a first-degree murder charge in the August shooting death of his former girlfriend, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Matthew Allen Waggle was taken into custody Oct. 5 on an active warrant and is being held without bond in connection with the death of Dawn Marie Kriskewic.

Deputies were called to the 500 block of 1st Street after 911 callers reported a woman lying in the roadway. They found Kriskewic with injuries consistent with gunshot wounds and began CPR before she was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she was pronounced dead. A judge signed the first-degree murder warrant for Waggle in August, and he was taken into custody at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office.

Investigators identified Waggle as Kriskewic's former boyfriend. A coworker told detectives that Kriskewic had expressed concerns about Waggle before her death and said he had previously threatened consequences if she called police when he came to retrieve his belongings.

Detectives said surveillance footage showed a person they identified as Waggle near the area around the time of the shooting, as well as walking through the area before and after it occurred. The footage also showed him discarding a shirt, which investigators later recovered. Near the crime scene, investigators found a rolling suitcase containing men's clothing and a tactical vest with a "security" patch. A Ruger pistol was found on a neighboring property along with a note stating that another person had given Waggle permission to use the firearm for firearm qualifications, according to the affidavit.
